title: envelope/safety.json — the ceilings, written by a person (2.1 rule 7, 10.3 rule 4)
description: Not a card and not knowledge: policy. A person writes it after confirming the limits outside the system, no agent may edit it (Tier 3), and nothing in it is transferred from anywhere else -- a safety limit written for another setup is reference material, not grounds. This schema exists because the file would otherwise be invisible: a JSON object with neither `card` nor `artifact` is skipped by the collector, so a mistyped key would leave check_budget returning `unavailable`, every run falling to Tier 2, and nothing reporting an error. The same silence held run logs until run_log.schema.json. The shape here is not invented: it is what simulation_agent/src/operator.py and axis_a5_budget.py already read.

policy_version.description: Recorded into every run log as safety_policy_version. Policy changes, so a run has to say which one it ran under; raise this whenever a ceiling moves, or the record cannot be read back.

written_by.description: The person who confirmed these limits. Not machine-read, and kept anyway: P0 rule 7 makes the confirmation the point, and a policy nobody signed is a preference.

basis.description: What the ceilings were chosen against -- which machine, what else it has to keep doing. A number without this cannot be revisited, only replaced.

targets.description: One row per place a run may execute. A second target is a data change here and not a code change: the cost model picks the smallest target that fits, and `intent` on the goal card decides between those that do (4.5.1). The target is deliberately not a capabilities/ configuration -- local and cluster run the same model and produce the same observable.

agent.description:
Which agent's limits this file carries. A discriminator rather than an inference from the path, so the file says what it is and check 5 can catch one agent's limits sitting in another's tree.

Narrowed to `microscope` on 2026-09-22. The simulation half moved to envelope_budget.schema.json on 2026-09-20 and this enum kept the old door open: a simulation envelope could have validated against either, and the two demand different things on purpose -- this schema requires `confirmation` because P0 rule 7 makes a safety ceiling the person's, and envelope_budget requires `chosen_by` because a budget is not a safety limit. A file could have taken the person's-only shape by naming the wrong artifact. Found by counting which declared properties no artifact on disk carries: the three simulation ceilings came up unused, and they were unused because the split left them behind.

limit.description: A ceiling. value and unit only: this is a decision, not a measurement, so it carries no source and no grade -- P2's four parts describe a claim about the world, and a policy is not one. What it does carry is `confirmation` -- not a grade, but the record of whether anyone physically checked this particular ceiling (10.3 rule 4, tightened 2026-09-19). As of 2026-09-20 a limit is EITHER a constant (`value`+`unit`) OR a lookup (`resolved_from`), never both and never neither. The two guard different events: a constant backstop catches a run that has already gone wrong, and a resolved ceiling binds in ordinary operation, every time. One file held only the first shape, so the second was being written as a number that was right for one objective.

unit.description: must be in units.json with a fixed SI factor, or si() refuses it

confirmation.description:
How this particular ceiling came to be in this file. Required per limit, not per file: a file-level `written_by` is the bulk stamp -- one signature covering twelve limits and saying which of them anyone actually checked. Librarian rule 10 already says a confirmation applied in bulk is not a confirmation, and if that holds for a KB entry it holds harder for the file P0 hands to deterministic code.

Copying a limit from another document is NOT forbidden. Forbidding it would mean confirming every limit before the file can exist, and then nobody starts the file. What is required is that the two be DISTINGUISHABLE, so a later check can say `an unconfirmed limit is parameterising an irreversible action` (2.1 rule 3's shape), which today it cannot.

This is not a grade. 10.3 rule 4 keeps a limit a policy with no source and no grade, and that is unchanged: the ceiling is a decision about what is allowed. What is recorded here is the EVENT of confirming, and an event is something that happened rather than something claimed.

oneOf.$comment: Confirmed physically, outside the system, as 10.3 rule 4 requires.

how.description: what was actually done. `confirmed` is not a how -- the point is that someone reading this later can tell whether the check would catch the thing the limit exists to catch.

oneOf.$comment: Carried from another document without being re-confirmed here. Legal, and visibly so.

from.description: the document it was taken from

resolved_from.description:
A bound that is a LOOKUP rather than a constant. Added 2026-09-20 for the objective focus ceiling: the rule is `do not drive past the working distance of the objective in use`, and there is no single number for it -- the six objectives on this stand run from 20 mm to 130 um, a factor of 150. Writing one number would be right for one lens and wrong for five.

**This does not put knowledge into envelope/safety. 10.3 rule 4 stands.** What the person writes is the POLICY -- that focus is the ceiling -- and that is a decision only they can make. The numbers stay in the store as graded vendor facts and are resolved at preflight. Nothing crosses; the limit names where to look instead of copying what is there, which is the same reason an envelope holds a snapshot rather than the store.

`confirmation` is still required and still means what it meant. For a resolved limit, `physical` says someone checked that the catalogue value is where this lens actually focuses on this bench; `carried_over` says it is the catalogue's word and nobody has checked. Those are different states and the second is the honest one until someone does it.

quantity.description: the quantity name the bound reads, e.g. working_distance

keyed_by.description: what selects which value -- the configuration or part that is in use
keyed_by.$comment: KEYED_BY IS PROSE, AND THAT IS WHY NOTHING CAN CHECK THE LOOKUP. Measured 2026-09-20, the day the first one landed. microscope_agent/envelope/safety.json sets objective_clearance_min to resolve `working_distance` keyed by "the objective in the nosepiece position the plan drives to". Five of the six objectives carry `working_distance`. The sixth, objective_mrd77400 (40x WI), carries `working_distance_min` 0.16 and `working_distance_max` 0.2 instead, because a correction collar moves it -- so for that one lens the lookup resolves to NOTHING. A check in contracts/ can count the carriers of a quantity; it cannot tell that the key domain has six members and five are covered, because the domain is stated in a sentence. Naming a registry here instead of describing one would make the domain enumerable and the shortfall checkable. Not changed today: envelope/safety.json is the person's file (2.1 rule 7) and this would be a rewrite of it, which is theirs. Recorded here so the next seat does not write a check that passes by counting five. What guards it meanwhile is the operator's own resolution failing closed, which is microscope_agent/src/operator.py and not this file -- check 57 does not cover it, since 57 asks whether a limit's confirmation is `physical` and says nothing about whether the limit RESOLVES.

fallback.description:
Names to try, in order, when `quantity` does not resolve for a key. ABSENT MEANS AN UNRESOLVED KEY IS A REFUSAL, which is the fail-closed default P0 asks for: a limit that silently resolves to nothing is no limit.

Why it exists, 2026-09-20. `objective_clearance_min` resolves `working_distance` keyed by the objective, and five of the six carry it. The 40x water-immersion lens carries `working_distance_min` 0.16 mm and `working_distance_max` 0.2 mm instead, because a correction collar moves it -- so for that one lens the ceiling resolved to nothing and no backstop stood behind it. The store is right to hold the pair: a quoted range compressed into one value stops being a quotation, and which end binds is a policy choice that 10.3 rule 4 keeps out of the knowledge store.

So the choice is made HERE, by the person, in the policy file. Each name listed must be at least as conservative as `quantity` itself, and saying why is the note's job -- the schema cannot know which end of a range is the safe one. For the case above it is the minimum: the true working distance is at least the minimum at any collar setting, so a ceiling there is never passed before focus while one at the maximum can be.

bounds.description:
WHICH DIRECTION THIS LIMIT BINDS, as a field the code can read. `min` means falling below refuses; `max` means exceeding refuses.

It is here because the direction was knowable only three ways and none of them was readable at run time: the `$ref` to `$defs/floor` or `$defs/ceiling`, which lives in the schema and not in the instance; the `_min`/`_max` suffix, which is a convention a name can lie about; and a `$comment` saying BOTH ARE MINIMA ON CLEARANCE, which no parser reads. So `operator.py` carried a hand-written map from name to direction, and `objective_clearance_absolute_min` reads as a floor on a quantity called `objective_clearance_absolute` rather than as the second floor on clearance that it is. `microscope-1` asked for this after writing that map.

OPTIONAL TODAY AND IT SHOULD NOT STAY THAT WAY. Making it required would refuse the person's existing file, which is the deadlock that makes a gate something to go around. A consumer that falls back to the suffix should say in its own code that it is falling back, so the fallback is visible rather than assumed.

Getting it wrong is not symmetric, which is why it is worth a field at all: **zero in a ceiling permits nothing and fails safe; zero in a floor permits everything.** A limit read in the wrong direction does not merely mis-bind, it inverts.

oneOf.$comment: A bound resolved per configuration from the store.

target.description: One execution target and its ceilings. The frame is shared; `limits` is the agent's own, so one agent gaining a limit does not touch the other's shape -- manager-microscope's point, and the recurrence path of the defect this replaces.

microscope_limits.description: The microscope agent's ceilings, specified by manager-microscope 2026-09-19 with a ground for each. Ordered as P0 orders harm: people, then instrument, then sample.

optical_power_max.$comment: PEOPLE. A7's total_optical_power bound abstains on missing: [safety_power_limit], and trap_laser_power_has_no_software_path (E3) says the dial is a hand control with no software path -- so a written ceiling is the only control there is. 2.1 rule 4 presumes an output that has one.

objective_clearance_min.$comment: INSTRUMENT, and a FLOOR rather than a ceiling -- the smallest gap allowed between front element and sample. nosepiece_write_runs_no_escape (E3): a Micro-Manager nosepiece write runs no objective escape, so the incoming lens arrives at the height the outgoing one left, against working distances of 0.13 mm at 100x oil. The prior repository put its own travel range in a SAFETY.md and 10.3 rule 4 forbids carrying it -- that prohibition is itself the argument for this field.

objective_clearance_absolute_min.$comment:
INSTRUMENT, and the second of two guards on one hazard. The person ruled on 2026-09-20 that rising to the working distance is fine and past it is not, was asked whether that is one guard or two, and answered BOTH, asking for the names to be split. Only one landed -- and not by oversight: `limits` enumerates its names and there was no second clearance name to land in. The ruling existed and the place for it did not, which is why the surviving half read as complete.

The two catch different events. `objective_clearance_min` resolves the working distance of the lens actually in the nosepiece and binds in ordinary operation, every time. This one is a single number for all six and binds only when something has already gone wrong -- a wrong key, a mis-seated nosepiece, a bad store value, a resolver that returned something too small.

BOTH ARE MINIMA ON CLEARANCE, SO THE LARGER OF THE TWO BINDS. An operator that reads one and not the other, or takes the last it parsed, has one guard and a decoration.

The value the store implies is 130 um, the tightest catalogue working distance across the six (100x Oil, MRD71970), with the 40x WI at 160 um once the person's 0.16 mm ruling is applied. At 130 um it never binds while the lookup is right. Implied is not chosen: this file is the person's and the number is theirs.

stage_velocity_max.$comment: INSTRUMENT. The person's standing preference of 2026-09-19 is that relative motion is driven by the piezo stage rather than by steering the trap, and a stage running away in front of a 0.13 mm working distance is the same collision. A7 owns stage_velocity and abstains on piezo_bandwidth, piezo_settling_time and stage_max_velocity.

stage_acceleration_max.$comment: INSTRUMENT. Paired with velocity: a bounded speed reached instantly is not a bounded move.

illumination_power_max.$comment: SAMPLE. A3's illumination_power abstains on sample_heating_rate. Lowest in P0's order and still a limit.

exposure_time_max.$comment: SAMPLE. Dose is power times time; bounding one without the other bounds nothing.

piezo_x_position_min.$comment: INSTRUMENT. The piezo stage's X axis, on controller channel 1 by the person's statement of 2026-09-24, a statement and not yet a reading. Device range -100 to 600 um; the person prefers 0 to 600 um. OPTIONAL IN THE SCHEMA, so the file stays valid without it, and REQUIRED AT USE: the piezo wrapper refuses every command on this axis while either end is absent, rather than defaulting to the device range. The two ends are required together (dependentRequired below), because half a range leaves the other side open.

piezo_x_position_max.$comment: The high end of the piezo X axis. See piezo_x_position_min.

piezo_y_position_min.$comment: INSTRUMENT. The piezo stage's Y axis, on controller channel 2 by the person's statement of 2026-09-24, a statement and not yet a reading. Device range -100 to 600 um; the person prefers 0 to 600 um. OPTIONAL IN THE SCHEMA, so the file stays valid without it, and REQUIRED AT USE: the piezo wrapper refuses every command on this axis while either end is absent, rather than defaulting to the device range. The two ends are required together (dependentRequired below), because half a range leaves the other side open.

piezo_y_position_max.$comment: The high end of the piezo Y axis. See piezo_y_position_min.

piezo_z_position_min.$comment: INSTRUMENT. The piezo stage's Z axis, on controller channel 3 by the person's statement of 2026-09-24, a statement and not yet a reading. Device range -100 to 600 um; the person prefers 0 to 600 um. OPTIONAL IN THE SCHEMA, so the file stays valid without it, and REQUIRED AT USE: the piezo wrapper refuses every command on this axis while either end is absent, rather than defaulting to the device range. The two ends are required together (dependentRequired below), because half a range leaves the other side open. Z IS A COLLISION AXIS, and a travel limit is not a clearance limit: which piezo-Z direction approaches the objective is unmeasured, and objective_clearance_min binds piezo Z as it binds ZDrive.

piezo_z_position_max.$comment: The high end of the piezo Z axis. See piezo_z_position_min.

illumination_power_max_488.$comment: PEOPLE. The confocal combiner's 488 nm line, power at the sample plane, one ceiling per line: the person's answer on 2026-09-24 to which limit covers the confocal lines. Optional, so the file stays valid without it, and required at use: the confocal wrapper (card 036) enables no line without its own ceiling, and a line with none -- 405 nm today -- is refused. The measured objectives are named in the limit's note, and any other objective is uncovered and refused. A per-line name rather than the single illumination_power_max, because one number cannot bound three lines that differ.

microscope_limits.$comment: Only the two P0 ranks highest are required. Requiring all six would mean nothing can be written until every one is settled, and then nobody starts the file -- the same argument that made carried_over legal. A limit that is absent is not permissive: the operator resolves it, finds nothing and refuses.

ceiling.description: A MAXIMUM. Exceeding it refuses. Named `<quantity>_max`. Zero here fails SAFE -- a ceiling of zero permits nothing, so the mistake stops the run rather than allowing it.

floor.description:
A MINIMUM. Falling below it refuses. Named `<quantity>_min`. Zero here fails PERMISSIVE, which is why the direction is named rather than left to the suffix: a floor of zero permits everything. The same number is safe in a ceiling and is the most dangerous value in a floor, and on 2026-09-20 a floor briefly held zero -- objective_clearance_min, where zero means the front element may touch the coverslip, against a nosepiece write that runs no escape and a 0.13 mm working distance.

WHAT THIS SPLIT DOES NOT BUY. `exclusiveMinimum` stops zero and passes 0.001, which means the same thing. A schema cannot know what is too small for a given quantity -- that is a domain fact. So for a floor the `confirmation` carries more weight than for a ceiling: `physical` with a `how` a reader can judge is the only thing standing between a floor and a number that is technically positive and practically absent.

constant_floor.description: A floor that may not be a lookup. Every other limit may be either, and this one may not, because what it is for is being independent of the lookup: a backstop that resolves the same way the thing it backs up resolves is not a backstop, it is a second copy of the same failure.

piezo_position_floor.description: The low end of one piezo axis's allowed position, in um, a constant and never a lookup. NOT a `limit`, deliberately, because `limit` refuses a value of zero or below: that rule is right for a magnitude and for a clearance floor, where zero means the front element may touch the coverslip, and wrong for a COORDINATE. The person's preferred range starts at 0 um and the device's own at -100 um, so inheriting it would refuse the person's limit. Everything else a limit carries is kept: the same `confirmation`, and `bounds` REQUIRED rather than optional, since these are new names and requiring it refuses no existing file. WHAT A SCHEMA CANNOT SAY: that the low end is on the right side of the high end. A consumer compares the pair before use.
